headlines.title: 17-year-old suspect arrested in Fairfield Halloween store mass shooting
headlines.description: A suspect has been arrested in connection to a mass shooting inside a Spirit Halloween store in Fairfield, police said Monday. The shooting on Friday left a 31-year-old woman dead and six others wounded. Fairfield police in a news briefing said the 17-year-old suspect was arrested in Suisun City. The suspect faces murder and attempted murder charges, police said. “This event shouldn’t have even occurred,” Fairfield police Chief Dan Marshall said, adding the suspect committed a previous shooting last year. “(The suspect) was charged and served a few months in the juvenile hall. Apparently he was rehabilitated and he’s back out to commit this horrendous crime.” Fairfield Oct 31 Fairfield Oct 30 1 dead, 6 hurt following shooting at Solano Town Center in Fairfield

headlines.title: Bay Area voter guide: What to know about the November 2026 election
headlines.description: What to Know — Election Day is Nov. 3, 2026 California will choose a new governor to replace Gavin Newsom, who terms out after this year. The choices are Democrat Xavier Becerra and Republican Steve Hilton. Voters will decide 14 state propositions. Regional sales tax Measure RTM, the Connect Bay Area Transit Initiative, aims to increase funds for public transit. California’s Congressional District 11 race features Scott Wiener and Connie Chan competing to succeed Nancy Pelosi. Aisha Wahab and Melissa Hernandez will face off again after a special election in August where Wahab secured victory to serve the remainder of former California U.S. Rep. Eric Swalwell’s term. All 80 California Assembly seats are up for reelection, as well as 20 Senate seats. California’s general election is Nov. 3, with statewide races and propositions as well as key local races and measures across the Bay Area. Here’s what you need to know to cast your ballot, including important dates and deadlines, how to register or check your status, where and when to vote, and what’s on the ballot. In this guide: Key election dates Check voter registration status How to register to vote How to find your polling place What to bring to your polling place How to track your mail-in ballot Why is California choosing a new governor? 14 California propositions What to watch Alameda County What to watch Contra Costa County What to watch Napa County What to watch San Francisco What to watch San Mateo County What to watch Santa Clara County What to watch Solano County County election offices Key election dates The last day to register to vote for the Nov. 3 general election is Oct. 19. County election officials will start mailing ballots by Oct. 5. Ballot drop-off locations open on Oct. 6 Last day to register to vote for the general election is Oct. 19. First vote centers open for early in-person voting in all Voter’s Choice Act counties on Oct. 24. In person early voting locations in the state open on Oct. 31. Election Day, Nov. 3, is the last day to vote in-person or return a ballot by 8 p.m. Polls will be open from 7 a.m. to 8 p.m. Vote-by-mail ballots must be postmarked no later than Nov. 3. If mailing on election day, get a hand-stamped postmark from a postal employee inside a post office. Visit the California Secretary of State’s website for a full list of key dates and deadlines. Check voter registration status Voters can check their registration at voterstatus.sos.ca.gov to confirm their mailing address and voting status. How to register to vote California residents can register to vote in elections at registertovote.ca.gov. Note Oct. 19 is the last day to register for the general election. Same day voter registration window will be open from Oct. 20 up to the Nov. 3 election day. Visit caearlyvoting.sos.ca.gov for a list of early voting locations to complete same day registration. How to find your polling place Visit the California Secretary of State’s website, where you can input your address to find your polling location and see what is on your ballot. Voters can also visit their county elections office for more information. Scroll down to the Bay Area county election offices section of this guide for further contact information. What to bring to your polling place Voters usually are not required to show identification to a polling place worker before casting a ballot, according to the Secretary of State’s website. There are some instances when providing identification is required: Voting for the first time after registering to vote by mail and did not provide a driver license number California identification number or the last four digits of social security number are missing on registration form In these cases voters should plan to bring identification to a polling place or bring a copy of it with their vote-by-mail ballot. The Secretary of State says the following are acceptable forms of identification: Passport Driver license Official state identification card Student identification card Copy of recent utility bill Sample ballot booklet received from county elections office Any document received by a government agency How to track your mail-in ballot Voters can track their vote-by-mail ballot and confirm it has been received by using the state’s Where’s My Ballot? tool at california.ballottrax.net/voter/. Ballots mailed in may take a few days to appear on the website. Why is California choosing a new governor? Gov. Gavin Newsom terms out after this year and voters will choose between Democrat Xavier Becerra and Republican Steve Hilton, who both advanced to the general election after a wild primary. Becerra has served as former President Joe Biden’s top health official and oversaw the response to the coronavirus pandemic. He was also the California’s attorney general during President Donald Trump’s first term and has more than two decades of experience as a congressmember. Hilton was a conservative commentator with a show on Fox News for six years. He also worked as an adviser to former British prime minister David Cameron. What are the 14 California propositions voters will decide in the November election? Here’s a list of the California propositions on the November ballot. Use the expandable graphic below for a breakdown on what to know about each measure. 2026 California Ballot Propositions Click on a proposition to see more information about what will happen if it does or doesn’t pass. Source: NBC Staff Reports • Interactive: Annetta Stogniew Regional measure to watch Measure RTM: The Connect Bay Area Transit Initiative, is a regional sales tax aimed at increasing funds for public transit. It includes 5 Bay Area counties: Alameda, Contra Costa, San Francisco, San Mateo, and Santa Clara. Races and measures to watch in Alameda County California Congressional District 14: California lawmaker Aisha Wahab and Bay Area Rapid Transit Director Melissa Hernandez will face off again to determine who will serve the next full two-year term. Wahab topped Hernandez in an August special election to serve the remainder of former California U.S. Rep. Eric Swalwell’s term. Swalwell resigned from Congress earlier this year after sexual assault and misconduct allegations. District 14 includes the East Bay cities such as Fremont, Hayward and Livermore. Measure X in Berkeley: Would establish 10% limit on annual rent increases and other changes to the city’s rent ordinance. Measure Y in Berkeley: Parcel tax to pay for arts projects. Measure Z in Berkeley: Parcel tax to fund a public bank. Measure AA in Berkeley: Increase soda tax Measure EE in Oakland: Shift city to a strong mayor system. Measure FF in Oakland: Eliminate foreclosure exemption from property transfer tax. 🗳️ For a complete list of races and measures on the ballot in Alameda County and additional election information, visit the Alameda County Elections website. Races and measures to watch in Contra Costa County In Contra Costa County, several county board of education seats are open. In Richmond, residents will vote on a new mayor while voters in San Pablo will weigh in on Measure S, which would limit rent increases. 🗳️ For a complete list of races and measures on the ballot in Contra Costa County and additional election information, visit the Contra Costa County Elections website. Races and measures to watch in Napa County California Congressional District 4: Mike Thompson faces Eric Jones. Measure B in Napa County: Sales tax to fund wildfire prevention and open space preservation. 🗳️ For a complete list of races and measures on the ballot in Napa County and additional election information, visit the Napa County Elections website. Races and measures to watch in San Francisco San Francisco voters will weigh in on several open seats on the county board of supervisors and board of education. Proposition A: Give mayor more power to hire and fire department heads. Proposition B: Pave way for public bank. Proposition C: Increase the city’s annual contribution to an affordable housing trust fund. Proposition D: New barriers to placing measures on the ballot. Proposition E: Changes to city contracting. Proposition G: Reopen parts of the Great Highway to vehicle traffic on weekdays. Proposition H: Parcel tax to fund Muni. Proposition J: Eliminate foreclosure exemption from property transfer tax California Congressional District 11: Scott Wiener and Connie Chan compete to succeed Nancy Pelosi. 🗳️ For a complete list of races and measures on the ballot in San Francisco and additional election information, visit the San Francisco Department of Elections website. Races and measures to watch in San Mateo County Measure E in Redwood City: Limit rent increases. Measure Q in Half Moon Bay: Referendum to block proposed farmworker housing. Measure U in San Mateo County: Create independent commission to draw supervisor districts. For a complete list of San Mateo County measures and races on the ballot, visit smacre.gov/elections. 🗳️ For a complete list of races and measures on the ballot in San Mateo County and additional election information, visit the San Mateo County Elections website. Races and measures to watch in Santa Clara County In San Jose, incumbents Peter Ortiz and Bien Doan are up for re-election in Districts 5 and 7, respectively, and there’s an open seat in District 9. Races and measures to watch in Solano County Solano County Board of Supervisors, District 4: Mike Silva and John Carli face in a runoff in a district covering Vacaville and Dixon. Measure E in Solano County: New tax on data centers and battery storage facilities in the unincorporated county areas. 🗳️ For a complete list of races and measures on the ballot in Solano County and additional election information, visit the Solano County Registrar of Voters website. Races and measures to watch in Sonoma County California Congressional District 1: Mike McGuire will face James Gallagher in a seat redistricted by Proposition 50. California Congressional District 4: Mike Thompson faces Eric Jones. State Assembly District 12: Eric Lucan and Jackie Elward compete in a battle between business and labor. 🗳️ For a complete list of races and measures on the ballot in Sonoma County and additional election information, visit the Sonoma County Registrar of Voters website. headlines.title: Anthropic posts $17B quarterly revenue but losses continue in fresh IPO filing
headlines.description: Anthropic’s quarterly revenue swelled to $17 billion but it still posted a net loss for the latest three months, the artificial intelligence giant said in an updated IPO filing released on Monday. The San Francisco-based company behind the Claude chatbot also disclosed that it has committed to spend $895.4 billion on AI computing and infrastructure like data centers, including $70 billion that’s due to be spent in the next 12 months. The numbers were released about a week after Anthropic issued its original IPO filing in preparation for what’s expected to be a blockbuster Wall Street debut later this month. The document, like the earlier filing, shows the company’s revenue is growing but — like its AI rivals — profit is still elusive. Anthropic’s revenue grew by 13 times to $33.2 billion for the first nine months of the year, but it reported a net loss of $104 billion, including a charge of $94 billion for an accounting adjustment related to financing agreements. On a quarterly basis, Anthropic lost $23.3 billion on revenue of $17 billion. The filing gave no indication of how much the company ultimately expects to raise, or what the shares will be priced at when it goes public. Anthropic has previously said it will list its stock on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under the ticker symbol “ANT.”

headlines.title: Students reportedly overdose at San Jose school Halloween party
headlines.description: A possible drug overdose during an afterschool party at a San Jose school has left many parents concerned and frightened. Multiple sources tell NBC Bay Area the incident occurred Thursday evening when two students had to be hospitalized after suffering an apparent drug overdose at a Sheppard Middle School Halloween party. One source familiar with the case said it was an over-the-counter drug the students took. The school district was not disclosing Monday what drug the teenagers are suspected of taking. District officials said they have launched an investigation. In an email to NBC Bay Area, the superintendent said the district is limited in the specific details it can share and are taking the matter seriously. The superintendent also said the district is working to determine any necessary follow-up actions. Both students involved are seventh graders at Sheppard Middle School. Both students are out of the hospital and recovering at home, according to the superintendent. “This absolutely concerning. We are talking about teens,” said Harsha Ramchandani, a chief medical officer at Bay Area Community Health. Ramchandani is not involved with the Sheppard Middle School teens, but said over-the-counter drugs can cause serious harm if not taken cautiously — drugs like Benadryl and cough medicine, including Tylenol. “That can cause hallucinations, dangerous heart rhythms, seizure, coma, even death,” she said. Ramchandani said an overdose occurs when the body is not able to handle the drugs a person ingests. The doctor said there was a 31% increase in child exposure to Benadryl, according to the CDC. An exposure is when a parent or a school official called the National Poison Control hotline to report a child has come in contact with the drug.

headlines.title: 1 dead in Sunnyvale apartment fire
headlines.description: One person died in a Sunnyvale apartment fire Sunday afternoon, and investigators are still working to determine what sparked the blaze. Fire crews were sent to 1235 Wildwood Ave. about 12:30 p.m. after receiving multiple calls about a fire in the building. When they got to the scene, crews found a unit fully engulfed in flames and were able to evacuate residents, including people in the four units impacted by the fire, Sunnyvale Department of Public Safety officials announced Monday. One person was found dead inside the unit where the fire started, officials said. The fire was under control within about 40 minutes and crews prevented it from spreading to other buildings. The cause of the fire and the circumstances surrounding the death are still under investigation. No additional details were provided.

headlines.title: Supreme Court rejects Trump administration push to set aside thousands of California ballots
headlines.description: The Supreme Court on Monday rejected the Trump administration’s push to force California to set aside thousands of ballots from people the federal government claims are noncitizens, a decision that came hours before the final day of voting in the pivotal midterm elections. The high court refused to immediately intervene in a case involving 20,000 people the Republican administration flagged as likely noncitizens on the largely Democratic state’s voter rolls. The swift rejection capped a string of losses for the president’s effort to intervene in the election before the counting of ballots to decide who controls Congress in the last two years of his second term. No justices publicly dissented. “The Court rejected Trump’s emergency request without even asking the other side to respond,” California Gov. Gavin Newsom, a Democrat, posted on X. “Democracy won.” Several lower courts also rejected the Justice Department’s push to set aside the challenged California ballots until the voters’ citizenship status could be verified. And in a case that revolved around the future certification of Alaska’s election results, a judge did not even hold a hearing before dismissing a Trump-ordered suit to prevent a possible Democratic Senate win. The high court did not detail its reasoning in the California ballot case, as is common in emergency decisions. The justices previously rejected Trump’s push to restrict mail ballots around the country in September, even though the justices have sided with his administration in a series of other emergency docket appeals. California Attorney General Rob Bonta, also a Democrat, noted the administration’s legal losing streak in a statement. “Courts have now rejected the Trump Administration’s attempts to interfere in California’s elections not once, not twice, not three times, but four times — from the district court to the Ninth Circuit to the U.S. Supreme Court,” Bonta said. “This latest decision should put an end to the Administration’s attempt to disrupt California’s elections through emergency court orders.” Voting by noncitizens is rare in the US The Republican administration has prioritized identifying noncitizen voters this year, despite it being a rare problem. California officials said the administration’s list appeared to be filled with errors and said setting the ballots aside could effectively disenfranchise legal voters. Also on Monday in Washington, another federal judge ruled against the administration’s efforts to make last-minute demands of California election officials, finding they violated the U.S. Constitution. “The Executive Branch has likely violated the Constitution’s Elections Clause, which commits authority over election rules to the states and Congress alone,” Chief Judge James Boasberg wrote. Later Monday, ruling in a separate case, Boasberg declined to issue yet another order against the administration to cease the demands. He ruled that Democratic groups that sued did not have legal standing and that the issue already had been dealt with by states and the courts. The administration, for its part, said segregating the ballots was a modest request that would eventually allow legal votes to still be counted. Its push has faced not only the remarkable series of losses in court, but criticism for waiting until a few weeks before the election to make its demands of California election officials with a list that even the Department of Justice admits is not entirely reliable. During a hearing over whether to lift her order forbidding the administration from threatening to prosecute election workers who let potentially illegal voters cast ballots, U.S. District Court Judge Trina Thompson drilled down on reports of widespread inaccuracies in the Justice Department’s data. “Would you agree there’s a high error rate?” the San Francisco-based judge asked Kenneth Kao, a Justice Department attorney. “That’s a fair statement,” Kao said. “That’s why we ask for the registrars’ aid in verifying these are all valid voters.” At the same time, Bill Essayli, the federal prosecutor running the Justice Department’s Los Angeles office, said at a news conference he was highly confident the people on the list were not entitled to vote. “This isn’t speculation. This isn’t a theory,” Essayli said, later conceding there may be errors on the list. Californians have already been casting ballots for weeks Voting has been underway in California, a largely Democratic state, since early October. Each of the state’s roughly 23 million registered voters is mailed a ballot, and more than 6 million have already been returned, according to Associated Press elections data. “The DOJ’s baseless challenge was yet another attempt at federal overreach and voter suppression,” Kristen Clarke, the NAACP’s general counsel, said in a statement in reaction to the Supreme Court decision. “We will not stand for the Trump Administration’s bullying campaign, and we will continue to use every tool at our disposal to ensure the American people’s voices are not silenced.” California election officials have said that finding and setting aside the challenged ballots now would be logistically impossible. Lower courts swiftly sided with the state, with a district judge warning last week that segregating ballots would “wreak havoc” on the midterm elections and erode trust in the democratic process. “If the Executive can discount votes and threaten an ongoing election due to unproven allegations, then our democracy is in danger,” wrote U.S. District Judge David O. Carter, who was nominated by President Bill Clinton, a Democrat. A 2-1 appeals court panel upheld his order, with one judge appointed by Trump and another appointed by President Joe Biden, a Democrat, voting in favor. The third judge on the panel, also appointed by Trump, argued in a dissent that California’s unwillingness to separate the ballots encourages the “violation of federal law.” ___ Associated Press writers Sophie Austin in Sacramento, California, and Safiyah Riddle in Los Angeles contributed to this report. ___ Follow the AP’s coverage of the U.S. Supreme Court at https://apnews.com/hub/us-supreme-court.
headlines.source: Lindsay Whitehurst | The Associated Press and Nicholas Riccardi | The Associated Press

headlines.title: Golden State Valkyries reflect on winning WNBA championship
headlines.description: Golden State Valkyries players took time Monday to reflect on capturing the franchise’s first WNBA title in just its second season of existence. Despite ongoing celebrations since winning it all Saturday night in San Francisco, most of the players said the gravity of capturing the WNBA crown still hasn’t soaked in just yet, except for Finals MVP Gabby Williams. “I was in bed by midnight after the game,” she said. “I just wanted to be with my friends and family. I mean, the game was early, so we did party. It’s been very calm. I’ve just had a moment to kind of soak it in. I didn’t have any expectations, but if I did, I thought it would just be party and whirlwind and energy. I found a very, I don’t know, just like serenity in everything that I’ve just loved.” Valkyries fans will have the chance to celebrate the team during Wednesday’s championship parade in San Francisco. “I’m expecting them to show up, show out,” center Kiah Stokes said. “I want it to be Halloween again, like come in the costumes. I just want it to be a big party. Just enjoy the moment. Let’s celebrate. Let’s have some fun. This is insane. I just want to feel the same energy that we have in ‘Ballhalla.’ I want to feel that at the parade.” Golden State Valkyries Nov 1 Golden State Valkyries 7 hours ago Golden State Valkyries Nov 1 ‘Closer' Gabby Williams validates Joe Lacob's hype in Valkyries' WNBA title win

headlines.title: 2 dead, 2 injured in shooting at Monterey County's Moss Landing
headlines.description: Two people were shot and killed at Moss Landing State Beach in Monterey County early Monday morning and two others were injured. The circumstances around the shooting were being investigated by the Monterey County Sheriff’s Office Monday, along with California State Parks police. Spokespeople for the agencies provided few details about the shooting in a press briefing Monday afternoon near the scene on Jetty Road, which leads to the beach. Jetty Road and Moss Landing State Beach were closed to the public on Monday. Monterey County Sheriff’s Office spokesperson Commander Andres Rosas said the Sheriff’s Office was not yet ready to declare the deaths homicides and said there were several unknown elements to the case as of Monday afternoon, including a potential motive or identity of a suspect. Monterey County sheriff’s deputies, California Highway Patrol officers, and State Park rangers responded to a person’s report of hearing gunshots at about 2 a.m. The Sheriff’s Office had earlier said the shooting happened just after midnight. Two people were found dead at the scene with injuries that Rosas at first declined to describe. When pressed by reporters, he confirmed the two died from gunshot injuries. A third victim was found at the scene and was brought to the hospital with injuries that Rosas again declined to elaborate on, but characterized the injuries as not-life-threatening. A fourth victim arrived at the hospital on their own while the response was underway. Rosas said he was unsure about the nature of their injuries or their status as of Monday afternoon. Chief Ranger Mike Dippel said the beach closes at sundown, but a gate that would keep vehicles from entering the area is frequently left open because there are not enough staff to open it early in the morning. A nearby scene at the beach that appeared to have been a party was being investigated by the Sheriff’s Office, which is leading the case at the request of State Parks, but Rosas said it was unknown if the crime scene was connected to the site of the party. He said there was no active shooter in the area when law enforcement arrived, leading the Sheriff’s Office to declare there was no ongoing threat to the community. Assemblymember Dawn Addis, D-Morro Bay, who represents the area, said she was in contact with the Sheriff’s Office and thanked them for their response. “My heart is with those who are affected by this heinous violence,” Addis said in a statement. “We must continue to work to end gun violence, and I am committed to doing so.”

headlines.title: Opening statements begin in long-awaited retrial for Antolin Garcia-Torres in Sierra LaMar murder case
headlines.description: The long-awaited retrial for the man accused of kidnapping and murdering South Bay teenager Sierra LaMar began Monday in San Jose, as prosecutors and defense attorneys laid out their cases during opening statements. It has been 14 years since the 15-year-old Morgan Hill resident disappeared in 2012. Antolin Garcia-Torres, looking older and somber in the courtroom, was convicted in 2017 for her disappearance and death, but a higher court later overturned the conviction. The appellate court ruled that the Santa Clara County District Attorney’s Office should not have combined three prior kidnappings with the original trial. Prosecutor O’Bryan Kenney wasted little time telling the jury what he believes Torres did to the teenager. “He grabbed her… subdued her… he dragged her… he put her in the back of his car… He closed the door… And he drove away… and then… that morning… Antolyn Garcia Torres… killed Sierra. He killed and hid her body,” Kenney told the court. Kenney also explained that he will introduce crucial DNA evidence during the proceedings. “Sierra’s body has never been found… yet traces of Sierra were found in the car driven by the man right there… traces of that man were found on Cierra‘s clothes… traces of that man’s car… were found on Sierra‘s clothes,” Kenney said. Lead defense attorney Al Lopez countered during his opening statement by arguing that the DNA evidence is not conclusive and was not handled properly by investigators. Legal analyst Steven Clark noted that the defense faces a significant challenge in countering the prosecution’s narrative and making Torres appear less ominous to the jury. “What you’re likely to see is the defense saying ‘we acknowledge that Sierra is dead, but that our client didn’t do it and convicting him won’t bring her back to her family… do not convict an innocent man,'” Clark said. With opening statements concluded, the retrial is set to resume Tuesday as the first witnesses take the stand. On Monday, the prosecution showed jurors the last selfie LaMar took and the last text she sent to a friend in the moments before she disappeared, a simple “ye” when her friend asked LaMar to bring her stuff. Jurors also saw a picture of LaMar’s red shoes that dogs used to try to pick up her scent in order to find her remains as well as a photo of her cellphone that was found ditched in a field by her home. The jury also heard the 911 call from LaMar’s mother in the hours after her disappearance. Legal analyst Steven Clark said the recording was not only haunting but effective for the prosecution. The prosecution is expected to wrap up its opening statement Monday afternoon. The defense, if it chooses, can deliver its own opening statement. Witness testimony is expected to begin Tuesday. headlines.title: Bay Area beaches face dangerous surf this week as light rain returns
headlines.description: Bay Area beachgoers are being warned to watch out for dangerous waves and strong ocean currents this week, with hazardous beach conditions expected through Tuesday evening and again Thursday through the weekend. In an advisory issued around 1:40 a.m. Monday, the National Weather Service said that long-period ocean swells will increase the risk of sneaker waves and strong rip currents along the Pacific Coast. The waves can sweep across the shoreline without warning, pulling people into the ocean from beaches, jetties and rocks, forecasters said. The first period of hazardous beach conditions is expected to last through Tuesday evening. Another round is forecast from Thursday through Sunday. Waves could reach 13 to 17 feet Thursday through Sunday, according to the weather service. The forecast calls for a 15- to 17-second westerly or northwesterly swell, increasing the risk of dangerous surf. Beachgoers are urged to stay out of the water, avoid jetties, piers and rocks, and never turn their backs on the ocean. The weather service also expects light rain across much of the Bay Area on Tuesday. The interior Central Coast is expected to see little or no rain. Rainfall amounts are expected to vary by location. Temperatures, meanwhile, are expected to remain seasonal to slightly below seasonal through Thursday, the weather service said.

headlines.title: Fairfield community members grieve, call for change after Spirit store shooting
headlines.description: Some neighbors and community leaders came together in Fairfield Sunday night for a community vigil following Friday’s mass shooting inside a Spirit Halloween store. One woman, 31-year-old Constance Hages, was killed in the shooting. Her family members told police that she was pregnant. Six other people were injured. Sunday’s vigil, hosted by the Solano County organization Broken By Violence, was held to offer a safe space for people to grieve, pray, and process. News of Friday’s shooting felt especially close to home for many in the area who have shopped at the mall before or visited that very store to shop for Halloween costumes. “People don’t feel safe in our community,” said Joy Forte, president of Broken By Violence. “Just a simple going to get a Halloween costume or whatever, and people’s lives are lost, and people are impacted.” “Senseless,” she emphasized. Fairfield Oct 31 Fairfield Oct 30 The vigil partnered with local groups that provide resources, including Napa-Solano County SANE-SART, which provides forensic and mental health services. “One bullet moves through an entire community,” said Kari Cordero with SANE-SART. At the vigil, many people said they felt especially fearful or upset in light of several recent instances of gun violence in Solano County. On Halloween, Vallejo police said a man died after being shot. Also on Halloween, Vacaville police said a 15-year-old boy was shot and is currently recovering. “I’m tired of the pattern,” Cordero said. “Something terrible happens, we gather, we light candles, leaders step up to the microphone and say this isn’t going to happen again, and here we are yet again.” People at the vigil called for more funding for violence prevention efforts and staff, as well as more investment in community patrols. The Spirit store in Fairfield remained closed Sunday, with a small memorial growing outside the door. Fairfield police said Sunday that four of the six people who were injured in the shooting were still in the hospital. One of those people, a 19-year-old man, was in critical condition. Police have not made any arrests in the shooting or shared details about any potential suspects.

headlines.title: Person arrested after shooting across San Jose City Hall
headlines.description: A person was arrested after a shooting across San Jose City Hall on Sunday, according to police. Officers responded to a report of a firearm discharged on Santa Clara and 6th streets around 4:16 p.m., according to police. The reporting party had told police a person was shooting a firearm in the area. At the scene, officers found the suspect and arrested him around 4:20 p.m., according to officials. Police said nobody was hurt and the investigation is active and ongoing.
